title: Elina Svitolina beats Aryna Sabalenka to reach her first WTA Finals semifinal in seven years
subtitle: The Ukrainian won six straight games to close out the deciding set. Now the only former champion left in the draw faces Wimbledon winner Linda Nosková, playing her first WTA Finals.
author: ATHENA

paragraphs.text: Elina Svitolina lost the opening game of the deciding set against Aryna Sabalenka on Friday at Indian Wells. Sabalenka did not win another. The Ukrainian closed out a 6–3, 3–6, 6–1 victory with a forehand on her fourth match point, claiming the last singles semifinal place at the WTA Finals and her first since 2019.

Sabalenka had won their five previous meetings, including January’s Australian Open semifinal. She had also won the Indian Wells title in March. This time Svitolina used the pace of the Belarusian’s shots to send the ball back past her. The WTA recorded eight chances for Svitolina to break serve across the three sets; she took six. Sabalenka served better in the second set, Svitolina told reporters, but could not sustain that advantage in the third.

For Svitolina, who won the season-ending championship in 2018, the route back to its last four began with a defeat. Mirra Andreeva beat her in the opening group match. Unlike a Grand Slam, where one loss ends a singles campaign, the WTA Finals gives players three group matches, with the top two in each group advancing. By Wednesday, Svitolina was a set down to Karolína Muchová, who had won all 32 of her previous matches this season after taking the first set. Svitolina broke that streak and earned the chance to play Sabalenka for second place in their group.

Svitolina sees a difference between the player who won this title eight years ago and the one who has come back to contest it. “I try to go a little bit more for my shots,” she said in remarks published by the WTA. Against Muchová, 17 of her 22 winners came after she lost the opening set. Against Sabalenka, it was Svitolina who went after the short ball to finish the match.

Saturday brings a different test. Linda Nosková, the Czech Wimbledon champion, beat Marta Kostyuk and Coco Gauff in straight sets to finish top of the other group on her tournament debut. Nosková has won both her previous hard-court meetings with Svitolina. Their most recent match, in April on the clay in Stuttgart, went to Svitolina.

Nosková had already qualified before her last group match. Svitolina had to play three sets on Friday to join her. Asked about facing another big hitter on Saturday, Svitolina put recovery first. Their match is scheduled to follow the semifinal between Andreeva and Jessica Pegula. A win would put Svitolina back in the final for the first time since 2019; for Nosková, it would be a first.
